## Board unfreezing; the delay is runner contention, not a stuck dispatch

All SEVEN of my changes now carry LLM-Review +1 (2619 picked up its vote) and all sit at Verified 0.
Main has advanced to 457d9a20bed9 -- another session's change merged -- so changes are landing again.

APPLIED THE 'DID IT ACTUALLY RUN' CHECK rather than assuming Ver=0 means 'running', since a run that
was never dispatched would sit at 0 forever and look identical. All seven have STARTED messages
(09:53-10:37), so dispatch is real. But 2594 started at 09:54 and its LAST message is still that
STARTED, 45+ minutes later -- worth one more look rather than shrugging.

Cause: RUNNER SATURATION. Queue depth right now is 12 queued / 3 in-progress / 15 completed. Run
33860623295 (2594) is in_progress; run 33860531798 (2607) is still QUEUED after 47 minutes. The whole
board re-ran at once after the operator's rebase -- roughly 17 changes times six jobs each -- so this
is expected and self-resolving, not a defect.

That retroactively validates holding 3276/9ea3/bff5: three more changes would have deepened exactly
this queue for no information. The reasoning was 'adding changes to a frozen queue burns CI to learn
nothing'; the queue turned out to be the binding constraint even after the freeze lifted.

At three concurrent runs the backlog should take roughly an hour to drain. Nothing actionable until
verdicts arrive; lengthening the heartbeat accordingly rather than polling a queue I cannot speed up.
